purpose: Grouping of saved PPv10 scores by selection meaning, for reading whether the most directly about a category notes sort first where comparable saved masks exist.
caveats: Grouped from already-saved scores only. One call per case; no repeatability, numerical calibration, or general reliability is established.
Pairs and their order are predeclared assistant judgments, not user-approved gold labels. These are mechanical order checks, not an accuracy percentage.
Only the coffee group and the reading pair compare different notes. Every other pair is within one note, so cross-note ranking outside coffee remains insufficiently tested.
Tentative and related-content pairs are informational: small gaps such as 86 versus 85 establish no meaningful separation, and both orders can be defensible.

Masks are unchanged saved inputs from several extraction versions. Prominence is not mask correctness, category membership, truth, quality, usefulness, or personal interest, and nothing here validates extraction or hierarchy construction.
PPv10 is unchanged and not production-frozen. The production registry still freezes PPv2 and was deliberately not touched.

preserved_disagreements.text: The vacuum sealer was predeclared as a major focus (70-89); the score of 58 labels it secondary. The post also extensively covers meat preparation and animal feed, so the boundary is arguable, and no harmful cross-note ordering has been demonstrated from this score. Do not hide this, and do not add a prompt rule just to raise it.

open_questions: The missing evidence for the actual product question is cross-note ranking with comparable saved masks outside coffee, including substantial secondary mentions. Search saved extractions for those sets before proposing any new calls.
How several masks' scores combine when one note appears under a node multiple ways is undecided. No sum, max, or average rule is implied by this review.

groups.title: Coffee across notes
groups.commentary: The three predeclared clear cross-note comparisons order as expected with large gaps. The mostly-hashtag second-coffee post scores 88, so the result is not explained by a blanket hashtag penalty. No order was predeclared between R03 and R01/R02.

groups.title: Coffee shops across notes (predeclared tentative)
groups.commentary: The one-point gap establishes no meaningful separation. Both high scores are defensible: a rave specifically at a coffee shop makes the venue part of the point. This is not a demonstrated failure and not evidence for either order.

groups.title: Reading across notes (different mask scopes)
groups.commentary: Orders as expected, but the masks differ in specificity: bedtime-reading advice among many lifestyle recommendations versus reading as a focused subject. Related content only, not a controlled identical-meaning ranking test; do not equate the two selections' meanings.

groups.title: Baby update (within-note control)
groups.commentary: Same note, two hashtag-only selections: baby selections central, nostr selections incidental. Supports scoring selections together in complete context; says nothing about cross-note ranking in those domains.

groups.title: Mixed diary: audiobook change versus Brussels
groups.commentary: Clear pair ordered as expected: a developed topic over background detail to a gift anecdote.

groups.title: Product post: vacuum sealer versus previous FoodSaver use
groups.commentary: Clear pair ordered as expected. The higher score itself carries the preserved disagreement below: secondary rather than the predeclared major focus.

groups.title: Daily update: safety plan versus closing sentiment
groups.commentary: Clear pair ordered as expected: a developed plan and its motivation over a brief closing sentiment.

groups.title: Shared meal: meal sharing versus workshop context
groups.commentary: Predeclared tentative and ordered as expected. Education also frames the post, so the workshop score is defensible; the gap supports separating secondary from major content but is one pair only.

singletons.commentary: Guitars throughout a long capo/retuning question: plausibly central as a focused long-note control. No predeclared comparison, so it supports nothing about ordering.

separate_work.commentary: Another agent's one-call probe: unchanged PPv10 on the saved MPv3.43 mask Rise and grind in a coffee-bean note, meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor at reasoning high through OpenRouter. It had no predeclared semantic expectation and is not part of the two Astra evaluations above. A valid score is not semantic validation or a model comparison; the subject metadata saved alongside it is not the scorer's input.
